title: Joe Brady On the Bills-Chiefs Rivalry And More
headline: Bills hold walkthroughs on a short week before Thanksgiving at KC. Benford's injury status is vague, and Brady says he wants to get Shakir more involved.
summary: Brady spoke before a walkthrough, with the Bills on a short week ahead of Thursday's Thanksgiving game against the Chiefs. He praised Andy Reid as one of the great offensive minds and said every coach studies his offense. He played down the bad-weather forecast: the team's mindset is to "put the ball down and play," with only equipment and cleat adjustments and game plans tailored to conditions. He credited Steve Spagnuolo's defense and the Chiefs' young corners for challenging receivers on every snap. He called Kenneth Walker one of the league's best backs when on the field, though Walker has been out with an injury, and said stopping Walker and Emmett Johnson will take a group effort. On injuries, he said everyone would be out at walkthrough and be evaluated through Thursday. Christian Benford was noted as not practicing, with no specifics given. He said the team feels good physically. He singled out Khalil Shakir as dependable and said he wishes he got him more involved, and he said DJ Moore and Shakir benefit from each other's success. He also praised Travis Kelce and the team's captains.

injuries.detail: Brady said he is not practicing today (a walkthrough day). He said everybody will be out there and be evaluated through Thursday, and offered no specific diagnosis or game outlook.

signals.claim: Benford will be evaluated daily through Thursday; his availability for the Chiefs game is not confirmed.
signals.note: Benford's status for Thursday is unresolved, which matters for the Bills' pass defense against KC's receivers.
signals.quote: obviously not practicing today

signals.claim: Brady wants to get Shakir more involved in the offense.
signals.note: Brady called him dependable in the run and pass game and said he wishes he got him the ball more, which supports steady targets.
signals.quote: I didn't get him involved enough

signals.claim: Moore and Shakir are both healthy and playing together, and Brady expects good things when the receivers are all available.
signals.note: Moore scored a touchdown last week, and Brady framed his red-zone production as opening up opportunities for the other receivers.
signals.quote: when we're healthy and everybody's out there, good things usually happen

topics.detail: The Bills are doing walkthroughs instead of practice on a short week off a Monday night game. Brady likes the team's maturity and said they feel good physically and are focused on the mental preparation.
Brady said the team won't spend much time on the forecast, beyond equipment and cleat choices. Game plans will adjust to conditions as needed.
Brady praised Spagnuolo's scheme and the Chiefs' young cornerbacks, saying they fit the scheme and challenge receivers on every snap.
Brady said stopping Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson takes a group effort. He called Walker, who has missed time with an injury, one of the league's best backs when healthy.
Brady said Kelce has revolutionized the tight end position, calling his route running and timing with Mahomes impressive. He said the Bills must know where Kelce is at all times.
Brady said the captains, five of them new this year, are key to the team's success and to holding the standard through adversity.

title: Ben Johnson on preparing for Lions' playmakers | Press Conference
headline: Safety Elijah Hicks is out for Thursday at Detroit; Johnson shrugs off D'Andre Swift's fumble, vows to keep stressing the run, and praises Salvon Ahmed's recent snaps.
summary: Johnson opened by saying Elijah Hicks has entered the concussion protocol after symptoms appeared, so he will miss Thursday's Thanksgiving game at Detroit. He called the Lions a hot team that is 6-0 at home, with an offensive line that has settled in and Jared Goff playing the best football of his career. He singled out Jahmyr Gibbs as an offensive player of the year candidate and a major problem for the Bears' defense. He also praised safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph, and the Lions' interior defensive linemen. On Swift's fumble he gave no sign of a lineup change, saying only that Swift needs to hold on to the ball. He called Caleb Williams' Sunday 'solid,' with some ups and downs and an interception he blamed on a good defensive play. He said the offense will keep emphasizing the run game, naming Swift, Kyle Monangai and Salvon Ahmed, and that Ahmed has taken advantage of his chances. He was glowing about Montez Sweat's preparation since returning from suspension and about the immediate impact of Jeffery Simmons. He also praised Theo Benedet's development.

injuries.detail: Placed in concussion protocol after symptoms appeared; ruled out for Thursday's game at Detroit.

signals.claim: Will miss Thursday's game against Detroit due to concussion protocol
signals.note: Hicks is out, so Chicago's safety group will be shorter on a short week; this matters mainly for IDP and defense streaming.
signals.quote: so he'll be out for Thursday's game

signals.claim: Swift's playing time is not expected to change because of the fumble
signals.note: Johnson gave no hint of a lost role, but another fumble could change the backfield split, so keep an eye on his snaps.
signals.quote: He just needs to hold on to the ball. He'll be fine.

signals.claim: Ahmed has earned a bigger opportunity after his recent snaps in the backfield
signals.note: He is a small-sample but rising name in the Bears' RB rotation, and a potential deep-league pickup if his snaps grow.
signals.quote: he's taken full advantage of his right now

signals.claim: Ball security is a point of emphasis against Detroit
signals.note: Johnson was not worried about Caleb's play and did not see him as hesitant, but he wants fewer turnovers in a game that could be high-scoring.
signals.quote: Caleb played a solid game

signals.claim: Sweat is practicing at a higher level since returning from suspension and should be productive on game day
signals.note: Positive process talk about his effort and prep is a good sign for an edge rusher's production.
signals.quote: He's practicing his tail off.

signals.claim: Simmons will keep having a major impact on the defense in the back half of the season
signals.note: Johnson says the acquisition has fit in seamlessly, which is good for the Bears' defense and for his IDP value.

topics.detail: Johnson said the run game has lagged and the team has 'too many good players' for that. The fix is a commitment to the principles and continued emphasis, naming Swift, Monangai and Ahmed. The offense scored only three points in the second half last week.

Johnson highlighted Goff, St. Brown, Jameson Williams, LaPorta and especially Gibbs. He noted new wrinkles from Drew Petzing and John Morton's influence, plus more vertical seam concepts and exotic formations.

He called the strength of the Lions' defense its interior: D-tackles Alim McNeill and Tyleik Williams plus safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph, who is back. The Lions are missing Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson.
Johnson praised the young lineman as someone the staff doesn't worry about on game day, and said he is 'just scratching the surface.'
The game is on a short week, with Ford Field expected to be loud. Johnson said the players will relish the Thanksgiving stage.

title: Zac Taylor Meets With Media After Monday Night Football | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Taylor offered no usable player news after the MNF loss to Washington; the transcript is too garbled to support any role or injury signal.
summary: Taylor opened by calling it a tough loss in which Cincinnati had chances but did not capitalize, which let Washington stay in the game. He pointed to the turnover battle and to missed opportunities in the first half. He called a sequence late in the first half a big mistake: the team ran the ball twice, was left disappointed, and settled for a field goal, which gave Washington the ball back. He said Cincinnati found a good rhythm on the last two drives of the first half but did not finish drives coming out of the second half. He mentioned that the team had more success once it adjusted to what Washington was doing, and that it drove the field for a field goal to build some momentum. He gave Washington credit as a good football team that had played well over its last five games. A passing remark about more opportunity to extend plays with someone's feet is too unclear to tie to a specific player. The captions are heavily garbled, so no injuries or player-specific roles can be reliably identified.

topics.detail: Taylor called the late first-half sequence a big mistake: two runs, then a field goal, and Washington got the ball back with time to work with.
He cited the turnover battle and an inability to finish drives, especially after halftime, as reasons for the loss.
Taylor praised Washington as a good team that has played well over its last five games.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference: November 24th, 2026
headline: No injury news after the bye; Monken says the offense will spread the ball among KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston, Jerry Jeudy and Harold Fannin Jr. and expects a faster start.
summary: Monken opened by saying outside noise doesn't matter, only having the best Tuesday possible and getting to seven wins. He said the bye plus the Thursday holiday gave the team normal Wednesday and Thursday practices, so they came back early with a short red-zone walk-through on Thursday morning, and he feels good about where opponent prep stands. He praised the opposing quarterback Mendoza for getting more comfortable from his first start to his second, and spoke warmly about Brock Bowers from their time together at Georgia. On the offense, he said he hasn't seen KC Concepcion change since he arrived, apart from knowing the system better and being a bit more consistent on route concepts. He framed balance as distributing the ball to many playmakers, and named Boston, Jeudy (who has had a good stretch) and Fannin. He said Fannin is improving in all areas, mostly in technique as a blocker and in handling the length of an NFL season. After studying the bye-week film, he said the team hasn't run it, thrown it or been explosive early, and he expects to start faster over the final seven weeks. No injuries were discussed.

signals.claim: Will keep improving as a tight end, especially as a blocker, and stay a featured part of the offense.
signals.note: Monken's praise for his development, with only technique left to refine, supports a steady role in the passing game.
signals.quote: he's continued to grow their leaps and bounds

signals.claim: Will remain one of several receivers the ball is distributed to.
signals.note: The coach cited a recent good stretch, but he also described a spread-out target distribution rather than a clear lead option.
signals.quote: we have Denzel and Jerry's had a good stretch here and played good football

signals.claim: Will remain one of several playmakers the offense distributes the ball to.
signals.note: He was named as part of a distributed passing attack, with no promise of extra volume.
signals.quote: we have Denzel and Jerry's had a good stretch here

signals.claim: Will remain one of several playmakers the offense distributes the ball to.
signals.note: Monken said he hasn't changed since arriving and that defenses aren't treating him differently, so don't expect a sudden usage jump.
signals.quote: I haven't really seen anything different in him.

topics.detail: The team returned from the bye for a normal Wednesday-style practice on Tuesday, a normal Thursday-style practice Wednesday, and a short walk-through on Thursday morning before players leave for the holiday. Monken said the extra time let them self-scout and get ahead on opponent prep.

Monken said the offense hasn't run, thrown or been explosive early, with penalties and turnovers killing early drives. He expects faster starts over the next seven weeks while still closing games out.

Monken said Mendoza looked more comfortable in his second start and that offensive coordinator Clint Kubiak does a great job. He called tight end Brock Bowers rare and uniquely wired, and joked he hopes Bowers is still hurt.

topics.topic: Primetime and the earlier Thursday game
topics.detail: Monken said the defense was excited for the Thursday night game against the Steelers, which a divisional matchup added to. He said the team earned being flexed to Sunday night, though it is unclear which game he means.
Monken praised players for doing community events during the bye, tying it to character, resilience and grit.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: “We Still Haven’t Played Our Most Complete Game” | Press Conference
headline: Short week vs. Philadelphia on Thanksgiving: Jashaun Corbin is likely RB2, James Houston and Justin Barron have earned bigger roles, and the Ferguson/Barham/Winters/Locke group will be clearer after Monday's practice.
summary: Schottenheimer said the Cowboys are playing with urgency. Washington is right behind them in the standings, so the Thanksgiving game against Philadelphia matters a lot heading into December. He said the 51-point win over Tennessee showed what the team can do, but he doesn't expect that every week and said they "still have not played our most complete game." He praised Quinnen Williams as dominant and said Terence Steele and Tyler Guyton responded well to being pushed in open competitions. On defense the focus is doing the simple things better: tackling, communication, setting the edge and protecting the ball. He didn't give injury statuses for Jake Ferguson, Jaishawn Barham, Dee Winters or P.J. Locke. He said there were no setbacks Sunday and the team would know more after the first on-field work Monday. Winters has a knee contusion and moved well, and Jalen Thompson has been missed in the secondary. Jashaun Corbin will more than likely be the backup runner this week, and James Houston and Justin Barron have earned more playing time. He said DeMarvion Overshown is not in the doghouse and is being used as a versatile linebacker and special-teams player.

injuries.detail: Coach said no setbacks yesterday and the team will have a better idea after today's first practice run-through. He gave no status, and the injury report lists Ferguson as out with a knee injury.
Asked about him with Ferguson, Winters and Locke. Coach said no setbacks and more clarity after Monday's practice.
Knee contusion. He moved around pretty well yesterday and has had this before. Coach won't make a statement until he sees him move today.

topics.detail: The focus is doing simple things better: communication, tackling, protecting the football, setting the edge and using proper hand placement against Saquon Barkley. Scheme matters less than fundamentals. Mike Patton took over play calling last week and the coach's meeting time stayed the same.

The 51-point day came from a complete team effort and the offensive line, but Schottenheimer doesn't expect 51 points every week. He said the first Eagles game was one of the team's best complementary games. He expects Vic Fangio to have some new wrinkles this week.
The team has figured out its Thanksgiving routine. This week they will tweak start times and add some individual drills to get players moving. Practice time is limited.

He respects Philadelphia's offensive line, which has had many changes, and said the group plays to a physical standard. QB Joe Milton has great arm strength and is being asked to make fast decisions and get the ball out quickly. He said the team won't get caught up in rivalry provocation of Dallas' receivers.
The team stresses urgency and keeps a one-game-at-a-time approach. It is coaching consistency by reviewing examples of good and bad execution and finding the cause.

title: HC Sean Payton on facing Pittsburgh: ‘We’re playing a good team that has played really well at home’
headline: Broncos suspend RB J.K. Dobbins for the Week 12 Friday game at Pittsburgh for conduct detrimental to the team; Payton wouldn't say who fills in at RB, and the game is expected to be wet and windy.
summary: Payton opened by announcing that J.K. Dobbins is suspended for this weekend's game for conduct detrimental to the team. He called it a head coach's decision and refused to elaborate. He would only say Denver will "have depth" at running back and wouldn't say who is playing. The game at Pittsburgh on Friday is a certain weather game, with wind and rain. The team will practice wet-ball drills, focus on ball security and field position, and pay attention to footwear. Denver moved its travel up to Wednesday night to get a walk-through in. Payton praised Aaron Rodgers as a first-ballot Hall of Famer and called Courtland Sutton an unselfish leader. He said Sutton's quiet stretches come from the coverage Denver sees. He credited Evan Engram's work underneath and after the catch against deep zone coverage last week. He said the pass rush of T.J. Watt and the Steelers is a strength, especially at home, and that Denver will need a sound protection plan. He also said rotating offensive linemen "within reason" is possible, noting that Ben and Matt both played well. On Jaylen Waddle he stayed noncommittal and only said the team needs everyone making plays.

signals.claim: Dobbins will not play in Week 12 at Pittsburgh because of a team suspension.
signals.note: Dobbins is out for the Week 12 game as a disciplinary decision, so he should be benched in fantasy lineups.
signals.quote: I'm suspending JK Dobbins for this weekend's game conduct detrimental.

signals.claim: Coleman remains a key part of the running game with Dobbins suspended.
signals.note: With Dobbins out and Payton praising the run game, Coleman is positioned for a larger share of the backfield work. Payton gave no names for the RB depth.
signals.quote: These guys run the ball exceptionally well

signals.claim: Engram will keep getting underneath targets against zone coverage.
signals.note: Payton credited Engram's underneath catches and run-after-catch for beating deep zone looks, which supports his target volume.
signals.quote: he did a great job of that.

signals.note: Payton praised Sutton's unselfishness but said coverage dictates who gets the ball. His target share can be uneven even when he is a main option.
signals.quote: consistency of leadership and work ethic is something that I really appreciate

signals.note: Asked whether Waddle is pressing after some drops, Payton gave a general answer that the team needs all its receivers to make plays. He gave no specific role change.
signals.quote: need all those guys to make plays

signals.claim: Early play calls are driven by the opposing defense's design, not by a plan to force Nix to throw to the middle of the field.
signals.note: Payton said some game-plan elements carry over from last week, and some plays not used then may come up against Pittsburgh's zone elements.
signals.quote: probably more design, defensive design and then how to attack it.

topics.detail: Payton called it a certain weather game with wind and rain, so footing and shoes matter. Denver will practice wet-ball drills and emphasize ball security and field position. The team will travel Wednesday night instead of Thursday, with a walk-through planned there.

Payton called Pittsburgh's edge players, including T.J. Watt, a strength, especially if Denver falls behind the chains. He said pressure packages are easier to dial up at home, so protection planning on the road is important.

Payton said rotating an offensive lineman could help within reason and noted that Ben and Matt's snaps were both really good last week. He said each has strengths and weaknesses. Which two players he meant, and what the rotation would look like, is not clear.

Payton called Rodgers a first-ballot Hall of Famer with exceptional arm angles and rhythm, and said he respects his longevity. He also mentioned his respect for Mike Tomlin and his friendship with Mike McCarthy.
Payton stressed a halftime lead and a fast start, even for a Friday game. He said Denver may have been under center more last week, possibly because of the four-minute offense.

title: Campbell on playing on Thanksgiving
headline: Lions DT Skyler Gill-Howard is out for the year with a knee injury. Juice Scruggs has locked down center, and Chuck Clark is a game-time decision for Thanksgiving.
summary: Campbell opened with an injury update on a player the captions never name, who is improving and ran around well Monday but could be a game-time decision for Thursday. He then discussed a player on IR, probably Cade Mays, saying they expect him back this year. The injury would have cost him the next two games, possibly three, so the IR move bought a roster spot. Campbell praised Juice Scruggs, who arrived as a utility lineman with starts at guard and center. He has become the center since the Mays injury and keeps getting better. On Thanksgiving, he said the main challenge is family and friends in town, and he expects a veteran team to stay focused. He praised Trevor Nowaske as a hard worker and fast learner who can fill many roles, after the team lost him and then got him back. Rookie DT Skyler Gill-Howard is out for the year with a knee injury that needs surgery, suffered on a goal-line offensive rep. Defensive tackle snaps should go to McNeill, Tyleik Williams, Levi Onwuzurike and Tyler Lacy, among others. Chuck Clark is a game-time decision, and Campbell gave no availability for other players who missed Monday's practice.

Did not practice Monday. Campbell said his availability will be a game-time decision.
The captions never name him, but he appears to be the IR player. Campbell said they'd like to believe he returns this year, and the injury would have cost him the next two or three games.

topics.detail: Campbell said the main challenge on a holiday short week is family and friends in town. Players must stay locked in, and he believes this veteran group has been through it before.
With Gill-Howard out, Campbell named McNeill, Tyleik Williams, Onwuzurike and Lacy as options, plus a couple of other possible fill-ins.
Campbell said he always saw Johnson's vision for football, concepts and detail from their Dolphins days.

title: Andy Reid on Buffalo Matchup: 'Heck of an Enviornment for a Football Game' | Press Conference 11/24
headline: Kenneth Walker III is moving toward a return and may test his groin in practice, and Trey Smith could be back on the line. Josh Downs keeps getting a bigger role ahead of Thursday's road game at Buffalo.
summary: Reid opened by saying Jaylon Moore (improving) and Ben VanSumeren (sprained knee) would not practice Tuesday. He called Buffalo a good, familiar opponent in a tough road environment on a short Thanksgiving week. Kenneth Walker III will get on the field to move around, but Reid isn't expecting much work and wants to see how he feels. Reid said Walker is feeling pretty good. Trey Smith is expected to practice and Reid said there's a chance he plays, which matters for the offensive line. Reid praised Josh Downs for absorbing more of the offense each week and said Mahomes is happy with him. Reid said play action is working because the linebackers have to react, with the backs and offensive line doing a good job, but he stressed that Buffalo's defensive line and active linebackers make it important to handle it right this week. He shrugged off Josh Allen not running last week, calling him dangerous whether he runs or throws. Reid also said the team is preparing for rain, cold and wind, and stressed classroom work and recovery on the short week.

injuries.detail: Will get out and move around at practice, but Reid isn't expecting much work. Reid says he feels pretty good; Thursday availability will depend on how he moves.
Expected to practice Tuesday. Reid said there's a chance he plays Thursday.
Won't practice Tuesday; Reid described him as improving.
Sprained knee; won't practice Tuesday.

signals.claim: Will go out in practice Tuesday for light work, and his Thursday status depends on how he moves.
signals.note: Walker looks to be progressing from his groin injury, but his Thursday status is still undecided, so wait for the practice report.
signals.quote: He's feeling pretty good though.

signals.claim: Will practice Tuesday and has a chance to play Thursday at Buffalo.
signals.note: Smith's return would help the interior line in pass protection and the run game against a strong Buffalo front.
signals.quote: I think he'll probably be in there you know.

signals.claim: Downs' role in the offense keeps growing, with more added again this week.
signals.note: Downs is gaining the coaches' and Mahomes' trust and is a rising target in the passing game.
signals.quote: every week we've given him a little bit more.

topics.detail: Reid said the keys on a Thursday turnaround are classroom prep and recovery in the training room, since practice time is limited. He called playing on Thanksgiving an honor.
Conditions are expected to be rainy, cold and windy. Reid said the team practices in the rain whenever it can, that both teams deal with the weather, and he gave no sign of changing the plan.

Reid said linebackers react to the run fake and then have to recover, which helps play action. He credited the backs and the offensive line, but said Buffalo's good front and active linebackers make it important to execute well.

Buffalo gives a lot of different looks, plays hard and fast, and has a good front and a smart defensive coordinator. The coaching change has been smooth because it came from within. Reid wouldn't speculate on why Josh Allen didn't run last week and said Allen is talented as both a runner and a passer.
Fred Johnson was elevated to the active roster. Reid said he has had enough time to possibly play Thursday, calling him sharp and experienced, but didn't commit.

title: Head Coach Mike Vrabel 11/24: "Wins are more important than any stat"
headline: Drake Maye is apparently sidelined and Mike Vrabel wouldn't discuss him. Tommy DeVito looks set to play QB, with Kyle Williams a familiar target.
summary: Vrabel said little about injuries or lineup decisions and mostly talked about accountability and execution. The defense gave up about 80 points in two games, and his answer was that everyone has to do everything a little better. He praised Tommy DeVito's energy, his work with the receivers and his improvement in fundamentals. He explained that DeVito's last appearance went badly partly because he moved from running the show team to facing live pass rush and blitzes. He said Kyle Williams and the other receivers will all play and need to be more consistent. Vrabel pointed to turnovers, self-inflicted wounds, field goals instead of touchdowns and big plays allowed as the team's problems, and said the identity is only as good as the 11 players on the field. He said defenders have to do their job even if it doesn't earn them a stat, and that wins matter more than stats. He had no regrets about the receiver moves and said the team will rally behind the guys it has. He declined to talk about Drake Maye's feelings or their conversations. He also praised Omarion Hampton and Mike McDaniel's run game ahead of the next opponent.

injuries.detail: A reporter described this as Maye's first prolonged absence as a quarterback. Vrabel declined to discuss Maye's spirits or their conversations and gave no medical or return timeline.

signals.claim: DeVito is preparing to play quarterback with Maye absent and is expected to be decisive and get the offense into the right plays.
signals.note: DeVito appears to be the quarterback the offense is built around right now, though Vrabel never explicitly named him the starter and the pass rush exposed him last time.
signals.quote: I think he's taken advantage of his opportunities.

signals.claim: Williams will play and is expected to be a target for DeVito, given their practice-rep chemistry.
signals.note: Williams has built chemistry with DeVito, which could make him a more reliable target if DeVito is under center.
signals.quote: all those guys will play.

topics.detail: After giving up about 80 points and nearly 1,000 yards in two games, Vrabel gave no specific fix beyond doing everything a little better. He stressed doing your job without chasing stats, such as playing tight man coverage rather than gambling for interceptions.

Vrabel wants consistency and no snowballing after a bad play. He wants fewer turnovers and self-inflicted wounds, and more finished drives and early positive plays. He called the identity inconsistent: wins mean it was good enough, losses mean it wasn't. He said the team has to start up front at the line of scrimmage.
Vrabel said he had no regrets about the receiver moves and that the team will rally behind the players it has.

A quarterback named Barron has improved through Saturday workouts and seven-on-seven sessions on the practice squad. Vrabel said third-string quarterbacks get few practice reps, so the team compensates with game-plan walkthroughs.

Vrabel called Omarion Hampton a physical runner with good contact balance who breaks tackles. He said Mike McDaniel's offense relies on outside zone, toss crack and some gap schemes, with motion and shifts at the point of attack, plus misdirection and insert plays. He noted they have run for about 150 yards a game over the last three games.

title: WATCH: Mike McCarthy Media Availability (Nov. 24)
headline: Steelers need to fix pass protection (~20 pressures and hits vs. PHI) and run more before a short-week Friday game vs. Denver. Highsmith and Herbig appear to be missing, which puts Jack Sawyer in line for more pass-rush work.
summary: McCarthy said the team is locking back in after losing two straight. It is a short week with a Friday game, so the Philadelphia corrections are built into the Tuesday and Wednesday installs. He pointed to protection as the starting point of the passing game, noting that Aaron Rodgers took close to 20 pressures and hits last game, and that Denver ranks among the league's best pass-rushing teams over the last two years. He said the offense needs to run the ball more, since good run games start with attempts, and that more run-action passing and better productivity should follow. He blamed the slow starts mainly on first third-down conversions and on a fourth-and-1 that was not executed well. On run-game struggles, he said the issue is how fast the linemen come off double teams to the second level, and that the run-blocking unit does better when it is intact. He praised Rodgers' wealth of experience and said they spent part of the morning going through past games. He described Vance Joseph's Denver defense as aggressive and excellent, and said the team looks forward to competing against Denver's top-tier defensive backs. When asked about playing without Alex Highsmith and Nick Herbig, he said young players like Jack Sawyer need to step up, since young players typically play in November and December.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 11/23/26
headline: WAS beat CIN on a late Jayden Daniels-led drive. Rookie WR Antonio Williams had his best game and made the big late plays. CB Mike Sainristil was out.
summary: Dan Quinn called the Monday night win over the Bengals one of the team's best, built on complementary football and turnover margin of zero. Washington's offense had plenty of yards but needs to improve on third down. Quinn explained he went for the lead on the earlier fourth down while still above the two-minute warning so Jayden Daniels would get the ball again, and Daniels delivered at the end of both halves. He praised Antonio Williams, who he said had his best game and was clutch, and the kicker, who went 5-for-5 on field goals. Defensively, the team used disguises and inside pass rush to slow the Bengals' receivers, though Cincinnati hit one deep ball over the top. Washington pressed Ja'Marr Chase more than Tee Higgins, mainly to set up good tackling after the catch. With Sainristil out, Rasul Douglas stepped up and Frankie Luvu made a huge fourth-and-one stop. Quinn said the defense under its two new coordinators has improved at tackling, communication and pressure calls as the season has gone on.
